native_result.query: What kind of demographic disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated?
native_result.HypoA: Gender disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated, with males having higher median wealth than females.
native_result.HypoB: Among individuals ever incarcerated (ever_jailed==1; jailed 1985-1994, n=289), median composite wealth in 1985 is much lower for Black ($320) and Hispanic ($0) than for White ($2,200) respondents, with 43-48% of minority incarcerated individuals holding zero or negative wealth; the White-vs-minority gap persists after deduplication (White $2,200 vs Black $1,030 vs Hispanic $1,380) though the Black-vs-Hispanic ordering is not robust. Ever-incarcerated women had $0 median wealth vs $1,000 for men (indicative, small cells). Within every race-by-sex group, ever-incarcerated respondents had far lower median wealth than never-incarcerated respondents of the same group. These are associations (1985 wealth of a cohort ever jailed by 1994), not causal effects.
native_result.WorkflowB: Filtered NLSY dataset to ever_jailed==1 (n=289). Computed median composite_wealth_1985 over all observed values (zeros/negatives included) by race, sex, and race x sex, with mean/zero-share/positive-only-median, deduplicated sensitivity (n=239), and never-jailed reference medians per demographic group. All outputs in analysis_outputs.json; full tables in analysis log.
